source.title: λ-Orthogonality Regularization for Compatible Representation Learning
source.authors: Simone Ricci; Niccoló Biondi; F. Pernici; I. Patras; A. Bimbo

record.file_problem: None; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether learned transformations make independently trained models’ representations compatible, using retrieval outcomes rather than a direct representation-similarity measure.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own retrieval results for mappings between model representations; these bear on mapped compatibility (V4) and on the extent of unadapted compatibility (V7). Statements about convergence and representation communication cited from other work are not recorded as results. The partial-backfilling ordering results do not test representation interchangeability.
record.test_reason: The study trains linear maps (orthogonal B⊥, λ-regularised affine Bλ, affine F) between frozen, independently trained vision models: ResNet-34 pairs, ResNet-18 to ViT-L-16, DINOv2 and CLIP. It reports cross-model retrieval through these maps, which bears directly on V4. It is a method paper, so the comparator rows and the tautological rows do not test anything. Its label-supervised contrastive loss also inflates mapped performance. The Table 11 L_B-only ablation gives a cleaner V4 test, but no row records it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that learned forward (affine) and backward (orthogonal or λ-regularised) maps align independently trained models into one compatible space. They find λ-Orthogonality balances downstream adaptation against preserving the new model's geometry, with λ needing tuning. They also report that their backfill ordering matches the new model with under half the gallery backfilled. They note the method assumes the new model is the stronger one.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired image embeddings and retrieval compatibility metrics, training affine forward and orthogonal or λ-regularized backward transformations with a supervised contrastive loss. It does not reproduce a direct cross-model distance-similarity or scaling measurement.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that the λ threshold changes the downstream/zero-shot trade-off and needs tuning; it states that different downstream domains may need different λ values. It also compares MSE and cosine distance for gallery backfill ordering, which is not a test of representation-convergence metric sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Unmapped embeddings of independently trained models (same or different architecture) give near-zero cross-model retrieval (0.04-0.10 CMC-Top1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently trained networks' embeddings are not directly coordinate-compatible; their bases differ, so a learned map is required.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the retrieval results. The study evaluates image-retrieval compatibility, not representation-distance convergence directly, and has no scale sweep. Its tests use a limited set of model pairs and do not isolate random-seed effects or explain why models align or fail to align.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit was not exceeded, but the selected rows prioritize the main ImageNet1K settings, the CUB200/CIFAR100 downstream settings, and the DINOv2/CLIP shifts. Other mapping-result tables were not extracted: Places365 extending-classes Table 5; DenseNet/EfficientNet Table 6; downstream Places365/Flowers102 Table 8; and the additional loss-component and backfilling analyses in Tables 11-14. The λ sweep in Table 9 is described as a method-sensitivity result rather than a direct test of convergence.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep of alignment.
No image-caption cross-modal alignment (CLIP is used only as an image encoder).
No same-architecture, same-data, different-seed comparison; the ResNet-34 pair differs in training classes.
Stitching, relative representations and maps learned without paired data are not tested. Only paired, mostly label-supervised linear maps are tested.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
No variation of the similarity measure or inputs for a convergence measure; Appendix G varies only the backfill ordering distance.
No rotation-invariant alignment level, plateau, or cause analysis. The unmapped near-zero retrieval only reflects basis differences.

missing.what: Loss ablation: L_B-only orthogonal map gives B⊥(ϕnew)/ϕold 62.75 vs ϕold/ϕold 55.62. L_F-only gives ϕnew/F(ϕold) 72.27. These are cleaner V4 tests without the label-contrastive loss.
Places365 ResNet-50 pair: B⊥(ϕnew)/F(ϕold) 38.50 vs ϕnew/ϕnew 37.37, and B⊥(ϕnew)/ϕold 35.47 vs 33.86.
DenseNet-121↔EfficientNet-B3: B⊥(ϕnew)/F(ϕold) 71.33 vs 71.60, and B⊥(ϕnew)/ϕold 67.23 vs 62.02.
Places365/Flowers102 downstream mapping results, including FastFill collapse on Flowers (11.12 vs 99.39).

record.verdict_notes: Method paper; the transformations are trained with class labels via a supervised contrastive loss, which can push mapped retrieval above either model's self-retrieval, so 'observed' on F(ϕold)/ϕold-type rows partly reflects supervision. For dimension mismatch, B⊥ truncates the larger embedding. No uncertainty is reported. V7 was relabelled untested: raw-coordinate incompatibility says nothing about rotation-invariant convergence. The paper cites the PRH and Li et al. 2015 (originals) only as motivation.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability scaling sweep measuring alignment across independently trained models.
No measurement of alignment between image and caption representations for paired multimodal inputs.
Independent models are compared, but the study does not systematically compare training seeds of the same architecture or assess shared features or subspaces.
Tests learned affine and orthogonal transformations with paired representations in image retrieval. Does not test stitching, relative representations, or mappings learned without paired data.
No analysis of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.

Does not test whether representation-convergence conclusions change across similarity measures, neighbour settings, or out-of-distribution inputs. Appendix G varies a distance used to order gallery backfilling, not a measure of representation convergence.
Unadapted cross-model retrieval is measured, but the study does not test whether alignment plateaus or whether shared data/objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain alignment.

relationships.condition: Orthogonal/near-orthogonal backward maps and joint maps for ResNet-34 pair, ResNet-18↔ViT-L-16 (ImageNet, CUB, CIFAR100), ResNet-18↔DINOv2
relationships.reason: Cross-model retrieval through linear maps reaches or exceeds the old model's self-retrieval and comes within ~1-4 points of the new model's (R03, R04, R14, R15, R25, R26, R36, R37, R47, R48). The Table 11 L_B-only ablation (62.75 vs 55.62) supports this without the label loss; that result comes from the text and no row records it.
relationships.display_finding: Cross-model retrieval matched or exceeded old-model self-retrieval and stayed within about 1–4 points of new-model retrieval, while an ablation without label loss achieved 62.75 versus 55.62.
